source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL: Program-aided Language Models
finding: The model writes a program for the reasoning steps and a Python interpreter does the arithmetic. This beat chain of thought.
numbers: GSM8K: PAL (Codex) 72.0 vs PaLM-540B CoT 56.9 (abstract: +15 points absolute). PAL run 3 times, mean reported.
limits: Needs a model that writes correct code. Gains are bounded by problem parsing, not by arithmetic.
agent_relevance: Core pattern: the model decomposes, code computes. Keep counts and sums in code, never in prose.

source: Gao et al. (2023) PAL: GSM-HARD stress test
finding: When GSM8K numbers are swapped for large ones (up to 7 digits), text reasoning collapses but offloaded computation holds.
numbers: GSM-HARD: DIRECT 19.7 to 5.0; CoT (Codex) 65.6 to 20.1 (about 70% relative drop); PAL 72.0 to 61.5 (14.3% relative drop). 16 of 25 inspected CoT thoughts were identical on GSM8K and GSM-HARD.
limits: Authors built GSM-HARD by editing programs, so labels rest on program correctness. CoT did not improve with large-number prompts.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that the failure is in calculation, not logic. Offloading matters most when numbers are large.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Program of Thoughts Prompting
finding: Separating computation (interpreter) from reasoning (model) raises accuracy on math and finance QA. A plain calculator patch on CoT text helped much less.
numbers: Average gain over CoT about 12% over 8 datasets: about 8% on math word problems, about 15% on financial sets (FinQA/ConvFinQA about +20). Zero-shot GSM8K: PoT 57.0 vs CoT 40.5 (GPT-3 175B).
limits: Mostly Codex. CoT+calc gave only mild gain because post-hoc patching has low recall. Gain smaller on SVAMP (about 4%) since it is simple.
agent_relevance: How the tool is wired in matters: computing in code from the start beats correcting numbers afterward.

source: Chen et al. (2023) PoT ablation: calculator patch vs program
finding: Ablation: an external calculator that corrects numbers inside CoT text gives only mild gains on math word problems, well behind PoT.
numbers: Exact table values not extracted; text says mild improvement over CoT, much behind PoT.
limits: Codex only. Cause given: rigid post-processing gives low recall of calibrated numbers.
agent_relevance: Offload the whole computation, not single numbers.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer
finding: A 6.7B model taught by self-supervision to call a calculator, search and other APIs chose the calculator almost always on math sets.
numbers: Calculator used in 97.9% of math examples. ASDiv/SVAMP/MAWPS: Toolformer 40.4/29.4/44.0 vs GPT-3 175B 14.0/10.0/19.8 and OPT-66B 6.0/4.9/7.9 (zero-shot).
limits: Table text was garbled in extraction; rows read from context. Tools cannot be chained or used interactively. Disabling calls still left some gain from finetuning.
agent_relevance: A small model with a calculator beats much larger models without one.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads
finding: Writing intermediate steps to a scratchpad lets models do multi-step computation they otherwise fail.
numbers: Polynomial evaluation: direct 8.8% (few-shot) and 31.8% (fine-tuned) vs scratchpad 20.1% and 50.7%. 9-10 digit addition out of distribution: no-scratchpad models fail completely; scratchpad models improve with scale.
limits: Scratchpad is the model's own text, so it is partial offloading (outside the forward pass, not outside the model). Needs scale or fine-tuning.
agent_relevance: Writing state to the visible page is the cheapest offloading and needs no tool.

source: Dugan et al. (2024) OccamLLM: Fast and exact arithmetic in a single step
finding: A frozen LLM hands arithmetic to a symbolic module in one forward step. It matches code-interpreter accuracy with far fewer tokens and no code execution.
numbers: Arithmetic average: OccamLlama 100.0; GPT-4o about 39.5; GPT-4o + Code Interpreter 99.8; Llama 3 8B 14.0; GPT-3.5 Turbo 20.7. GPT-4o+Code used over 50x more generation tokens.
limits: Arithmetic ops only. On the math-problem average GPT-4o+Code did not beat GPT-4o, so code tools are not always used well.
agent_relevance: Even strong models get about 40% on raw arithmetic with sqrt, log, trig. Never trust in-head arithmetic.

source: Li et al. (2023) Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator
finding: The model writes code; a real interpreter runs what it can and the model simulates undefined lines while keeping explicit variable state.
numbers: BIG-Bench Hard: 84%, about 12 points over CoT. Beats average human raters overall and best raters on an algorithmic subset.
quote: a gain of 12% over Chain of Thought
limits: Needs code-structured prompts; semantic steps simulated by the LM can still be wrong. Human baseline is BIG-Bench raters.
agent_relevance: Program state kept as explicit variables (delta state) is a working model of keeping state in code.

source: Gou et al. (2024) ToRA: Tool-integrated Reasoning Agents for Math
finding: Interleaving natural-language rationale with program calls, with imitation learning and output-space shaping, gives large open-model gains.
numbers: 10 math datasets: 13-19 points absolute average gain. ToRA-7B 44.6% on MATH. ToRA-Code-34B above 50% on MATH, above GPT-4 CoT.
limits: Trained on curated GPT-4 trajectories; gains depend on that data.
agent_relevance: Interleaving (think, compute, read result, think) is the loop shape to copy.

source: Bayat et al. (2026) From Proof to Program: Tool-Induced Myopia
finding: With a Code Interpreter, answers become more often right but reasoning gets worse. Tool output replaces derivation.
numbers: PYMATH: 1,679 competition problems. Accuracy gain up to 19.3 points; non-tool models win up to 41.5% more pairwise reasoning comparisons. Tool-induced myopia in 54.3% of high-risk cases. Errors shift from arithmetic to logic, assumption and creativity failures.
quote: TaLMs treat tool outputs as substitutes for reasoning
limits: Accuracy gain is modest for most models; GPT-5 used as judge; problems filtered to be TIM-prone.
agent_relevance: Offloading arithmetic may relax thought on the global plan. Add a check that the plan is justified, not only the numbers.

source: Bayat et al. (2026) TIM dose-response by tool calls
finding: The more tool calls, the wider the reasoning gap against the no-tool version.
numbers: Bins 0-3, 4-7, 8-11, 12+ calls: base-model win rate and miss rate rise, step-level PRM accuracy falls. Tool-use rate on PYMATH: Claude-Opus-4 99.8%, GPT-5 73.7%.
limits: 12+ bin has few samples and shows reversals.
agent_relevance: Cap tool calls per sub-problem; many small calls signal trial and error instead of a plan.

source: Bayat et al. (2026) TIM mitigation (prompt and DPO)
finding: A prompt telling the model to use tools as evidence cut myopia but cost accuracy. DPO on matched-correctness pairs improved both.
numbers: GPT-4.1 final accuracy: base 24.6, vanilla tool 27.0, prompting 25.1, DPO 27.6; win rate 58.2% vs base; miss rate 46.6%; step accuracy 83.3% still below base 88.6%.
limits: Small absolute gains; needs training, so not usable in a scaffold-only agent.
agent_relevance: Prompting alone trades accuracy for reasoning quality. A scaffold needs a separate check step instead.

source: Bayat et al. (2026) TIM by model and thinking mode
finding: Models with higher tool use showed more myopia; thinking models used tools on about 50% more problems than non-thinking ones.
numbers: Claude-Opus-4 and o4-mini higher incidence; Gemini models lower.
limits: Per-model rates are in a figure only.
agent_relevance: Strong tool users need the justification check most.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Acting Less is Reasoning More (OTC-PO)
finding: Names the model-side problem as cognitive offloading: RL on correctness alone causes excess tool calls. A reward for few calls cuts them.
numbers: Tool calls cut up to 68.3%; tool productivity (correct answers per call) up 215.4%; accuracy comparable. Qwen2.5 on NQ and HotpotQA.
quote: hindering the development of internal reasoning capabilities
limits: RL-trained search agents (Search-R1 baselines), search tools rather than calculators.
agent_relevance: Track tool productivity; overuse of tools is a real failure.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: The model pages information between a small context and external recall and archival stores through function calls.
numbers: Deep memory retrieval accuracy: GPT-3.5 Turbo 38.7 to 66.9%; GPT-4 32.1 to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3 to 93.4% with MemGPT.
limits: Self-built multi-session chat set; embedding retrieval can miss.
agent_relevance: External store for state across long runs; the model decides what to write and fetch.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Even with the exact solution algorithm in the prompt, reasoning models did not execute it more reliably in puzzles.
numbers: Tower of Hanoi and Checker Jumping: giving the algorithm did not raise accuracy; collapse stayed at about the same complexity. Thinking and non-thinking models reach near-zero accuracy at high complexity.
limits: Critiques say output-token limits and unsolvable instances explain part of the collapse (not opened). No code tools were given.
agent_relevance: Long exact procedures in text fail. Move step execution to code that returns the next state.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
finding: Zero-shot accuracy of GPT-3, ChatGPT and GPT-4 falls toward zero as multiplication digits and puzzle size grow. Models match subgraphs rather than run algorithms.
numbers: Accuracy decays to near zero with problem size on multiplication, logic grid puzzles, dynamic programming. Scratchpad fine-tuning helps in distribution only.
limits: Exact digit-level numbers are in figures, not extracted.
agent_relevance: Supports offloading long, exact, many-step work to code.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT
finding: Human study of offloading to an LLM during essay writing: weaker brain connectivity and poorer recall of own essays with LLM help.
numbers: N=54 in sessions 1-3, 18 in session 4. EEG connectivity scaled down with external support: brain-only strongest, search intermediate, LLM weakest. LLM group worse at quoting own essay.
limits: Small sample, preprint, EEG interpretation contested.
agent_relevance: Warns that full offloading reduces ownership and recall. Keep the plan in the agent's own context even if arithmetic is in code.

source: Salomon (1997) Distributed Cognitions
finding: Founding book for the subfield: cognition distributed across people and artefacts.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Frames offloading as a joint system, like a model plus code.

source: Risko and Gilbert (2016) Cognitive Offloading
finding: Review defining cognitive offloading as using physical action to alter task demands.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened; numbers deliberately omitted.
agent_relevance: Defines the concept used in the machine studies above.

source: Kirsh and Maglio (1994) On distinguishing epistemic from pragmatic action
finding: Tetris players rotate pieces on screen to think, not only to place them.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened; numbers omitted.
agent_relevance: Epistemic actions map to tool calls that reduce uncertainty.

source: Sparrow et al. (2011) Google Effects on Memory, and its replication
finding: Original reported people remember where to find facts, not the facts. A large replication project later reported failure to replicate the main effect.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Replication status from memory of Camerer et al. (2018); verify before use.
agent_relevance: Treat human offloading harms as uncertain; do not design from them.

source: Critique of Illusion of Thinking (2025)
finding: Reply argues the puzzle collapse is partly caused by token limits and unsolvable cases.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle
finding: Models use information worse when it sits in the middle of a long context, which motivates external storage.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports writing key state outside the prompt middle.

source: Qian et al. (2025) Tool overuse in LLMs
finding: Cited by Bayat et al. and Wang et al. as showing that unrestricted tool access can harm performance.
numbers: Not read this session.
limits: Seen only as a citation in c09 and c13.
agent_relevance: Overuse risk is documented by several groups.
